sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is the smallest of the known congeners in every measurement. It is closest to I. rhyzophorae, but the shaft of antennal segment 3 is more slender in this species; in I. rhyzophorae the anterior margin of the pronotum is deeply incised, whereas in this species the anterior margin is only shallowly concave. The alate is the smallest of the dark-coloured group and is difficult to distinguish from I. rhyzophorae, but the latter is known only from Cuba and the Bahamas.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Apparently monomorphic, very small. In dorsal view the anterior part of the head capsule is pale rusty, becoming pale yellow posteriorly; the basal 2 antennal segments are yellow-orange, segment 3 slightly darker and concolorous with the mandible base. Pronotum pale yellow. Mandible base dark chestnut, the apex almost black. Frontal suture a pale line. Eye spot white, its boundary indistinct. Postmentum pale rusty, genae pale yellow. Head capsule shining, the surface unmarked. In dorsal view the head capsule is narrow and elongate, its sides parallel or very slightly convergent posteriorly; the posterior margin slightly concave. Mandibles slender and elongate, the basal hump very shallow, the apex curved at 60°. Setae few, present only on the vertex and frons. Labrum prominent, subtrapezoidal. Antennae 9—10 segmented, usually 10, the relative length formula 2<3 4=5; the shaft of antennal segment 3 distinctly long, the apex broadly clavate, as long as the 3 following segments together. Anterior margin of the pronotum evenly and shallowly concave, without an incision, the sides slightly convex, the posterior margin almost straight. In lateral and oblique view the head capsule is moderately dorsoventrally flattened; the frons slopes at about 20° from the vertex; the frontal margins form a very shallow double convexity; the eye spot is broadly oval; the left mandible is moderately more upcurved than the right. Measurements (n=6, range/mean±standard deviation (holotype)): head length including mandibles 1.90—2.07/1.98±0.064 (1.98) mm, head length to the postclypeus 1.26—1.36/1.33±0.037 (1.31) mm, maximum head width 0.75—0.85/0.79±0.034 (0.75) mm, width across the antennal ridges 0.72—0.82/0.76±0.034 (0.72) mm, head height (excluding postmentum) 0.53—0.65/0.59±0.043 (0.57) mm, maximum labrum width 0.26—0.29/0.28±0.013 (0.29) mm, left mandible length 0.87—0.98/0.91±0.052 (0.90) mm, postmentum length 0.83—0.92/0.87±0.029 (0.85) mm, maximum width 0.35—0.39/0.37±0.015 (0.36) mm and minimum width 0.15—0.18/0.16±0.013 (0.16) mm, maximum pronotum width 0.78—0.87/0.82±0.032 (0.80) mm, maximum length 0.52—0.60/0.57±0.029 (0.59) mm, hind femur length 0.56—0.64/0.59±0.030 (0.57) mm and width 0.20—0.25/0.23±0.019 (0.23) mm, hind tibia length 0.57—0.62/0.60±0.017 (0.59) mm, body length 4.04—5.23/4.60±0.44 (4.77) mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: In dorsal view uniformly dark brown (dark sepia brown), concolorous with the sclerotized veins of the fore wing; wing membrane pale brown, without iridescent lustre. Frons and vertex dark brown, pale only in the minute pits at the setal bases. Pronotum and abdominal tergites dark brown. The median line of the thoracic tergites is indistinct. Basal 4 antennal segments very pale brown, the distal segments dark brown. Labrum pale brown. Legs (including the femora) dark brown, the tibiae and tarsi distinctly paler. Sternites pale brown, becoming dark brown distally. Head long and almost quadrate; coronal suture absent. Compound eyes very small, moderately projecting, slightly triangular. Ocelli small, short-oval, very narrowly touching the compound eye. Antennae 13—15 segmented (only 2 specimens), formula 2<3>4=5, segment 3 only slightly elongated. Anterior margin of the pronotum very shallowly incised, the posterior margin similarly notched, the sides nearly parallel; the transverse band and median line indistinct. The radius reaches the anterior margin of the fore wing at about 1/5 of the wing length from the suture; the radial sector has 7—8 branches; the first branch of the radial sector arises before the radius reaches the anterior margin. Arolia very small. Measurements (n=2, same colony, range/mean±standard deviation): head length including labrum 1.01—1.05/1.03±0.023 mm, head length to the postclypeus 0.82—0.83/0.83±0.012 mm, maximum head width (at the compound eyes) 0.82—0.87/0.84±0.035 mm, compound eye diameter (including sclerites) 0.27—0.28/0.27±0.006 mm, minimum distance from the compound eye to the head base 0.10—0.11/0.11±0.012 mm, ocellus diameter 0.07—0.08/0.08±0.003 mm, maximum pronotum width 0.75—0.82/0.78±0.046 mm, maximum length 0.57—0.64/0.60±0.046 mm, body length with wings 8.09—8.24/8.17±0.10 mm, body length without wings 5.11—5.25/5.18±0.10 mm, fore wing length (from the suture) 5.40—5.54/5.47±0.10 mm, maximum fore wing width 1.25—1.29/1.27±0.023 mm.

note: Adapted from the new-species description in Scheffrahn, Austin & Szalanski (2024), original in English; the header of the measurement table misspells the species name as I. marie; figure numbers (Figs 4—5), the holotype locality and collection records are not translated.
